name: George du Maurier
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: George du Maurier (1834–1896) was a French-British cartoonist, illustrator and novelist, known for his work in Punch and for the novels Peter Ibbetson and Trilby.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: Musk
poems.author: George du Maurier
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Kindly watcher by my bed, lift no voice in prayer,
Waste not any words on me when the hour is nigh,
Let a stream of melody but flow from some sweet player,
And meekly will I lay my head and fold my hands to die.
Sick I am of idle words, past all reconciling,
Words that weary and perplex and pander and conceal,
Wake the sounds that cannot lie, for all their sweet beguiling;
The language one need fathom not, but only hear and feel.

Let them roll once more to me, and ripple in my hearing,
Like waves upon a lonely beach where no craft anchoreth:
That I may steep my soul therein, and craving naught,
nor feeling,
Drift on through slumber to a dream, and through a
dream to death.
